security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples, not executable Ruby or shell evaluation. remediation.suggestion: Package the shared authentication and permission instructions inside this skill, or declare and audit the shared dependency explicitly. Avoid ../ paths in marketplace-published skill instructions.

remediation.issue: CLI examples can trigger noisy static detections
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples clearly labeled as documentation and avoid ambiguous backtick-heavy formatting where plain text is sufficient.

content.value_statement: Attendance records are hard to query when users must remember Lark CLI resources and required parameters. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to request the schema and query personal clock-in records with the required defaults.
actual_capabilities: Guides use of lark-cli attendance resources.
Queries personal attendance clock-in records through user_tasks.query.
Requires schema lookup before native attendance API calls.
Keeps employee_type fixed as employee_no for requests.
Keeps user_ids empty when building attendance query data.
Identifies the required attendance:task:readonly permission scope.
limitations: Requires lark-cli to be installed and configured.
Requires valid Lark authentication and attendance read permission.
Only documents the user_tasks.query attendance endpoint.
Does not edit attendance records or approve corrections.

use_cases.title: Check Personal Clock-Ins
use_cases.description: Review your own attendance clock-in records for a date or date range.

use_cases.title: Prepare Attendance Questions
use_cases.description: Confirm your own record details before asking HR about a missing or unusual entry.

use_cases.title: Validate Attendance CLI Access
use_cases.description: Test the attendance schema, readonly scope, and query path for a configured Lark account.

prompt_templates.title: Check Today
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for current attendance data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Lark attendance skill to check my attendance clock-in records for today. Confirm any required date input before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Date Range
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs records across several days.
prompt_templates.prompt: Query my Lark attendance records for [start date] through [end date]. Use the schema first and keep employee_type and user_ids defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate A Missing Entry
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants help understanding an attendance gap.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my attendance records for [date] and summarize any missing or unusual clock-in information. Tell me what data came from Lark.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Query Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that checks access, schema, and query behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the attendance query schema, confirm the required readonly scope, then query records for [date range] with the skill defaults and explain the command choices.

output_examples.output: A short summary of yesterday's clock-in records, any missing entries, and whether the query used the required defaults.

output_examples.input: Why did my attendance query fail?
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting summary that checks lark-cli setup, authentication status, attendance permission, and required parameter defaults.

output_examples.input: Show my attendance records for last week.
output_examples.output: A day-by-day attendance summary with dates that returned no data and any permission or parameter issues.

best_practices: Confirm lark-cli authentication before querying attendance records.
Run the schema lookup before using native attendance API parameters.
Keep employee_type and user_ids aligned with the skill defaults.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to request other employees' attendance records.
Do not skip the schema check before building attendance parameters.
Do not paste access tokens or session secrets into prompts.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps query personal Feishu and Lark attendance clock-in records through lark-cli.

faq.question: Does it require Lark access?
faq.answer: Yes. The configured account needs Lark authentication and the attendance:task:readonly permission scope.

faq.question: Can it change attendance records?
faq.answer: No. The skill only documents a readonly attendance query path.

faq.question: Can it query another employee's records?
faq.answer: The skill is written for querying the current user's attendance records, not other employees' data.

faq.question: Why does it check the schema first?
faq.answer: The schema check reduces parameter mistakes before calling the native attendance API.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
